source.text: Ἀδελφοί, κατὰ ἄνθρωπον λέγω· ὅμως ἀνθρώπου κεκυρωμένην διαθήκην οὐδεὶς ἀθετεῖ ἢ ἐπιδιατάσσεται.

records.literal_gloss: Brothers, according to man I speak; even of man having been ratified covenant no one sets aside or adds to.

en.L: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, I speak in human terms: even a human covenant, once it has been ratified, no one sets aside or adds to.
en.B: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, I will use an illustration from human life. Even a human will, once it has been made binding, is something no one can cancel or add new terms to.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, here is an example from ordinary life. When someone makes a will and it has been made official, no one can cancel it or add anything to it.

es.L: Hermanos, hablo en términos humanos: aun un pacto humano, una vez ratificado, nadie lo invalida ni le añade [nada].
es.B: Hermanos, voy a poner un ejemplo de la vida humana. Aun el testamento de una persona, una vez que ha sido validado, nadie puede anularlo ni añadirle nuevas condiciones.
es.R: Hermanos, aquí va un ejemplo de la vida diaria. Cuando alguien hace un testamento y este queda oficialmente registrado, nadie puede anularlo ni añadirle nada.

sw.L: Ndugu, ninasema kwa namna ya kibinadamu: hata agano la mwanadamu, likiisha kuthibitishwa, hakuna mtu anayelitangua wala anayeliongezea [kitu].
sw.B: Ndugu, nitatumia mfano kutoka katika maisha ya kibinadamu. Hata wosia wa mtu, ukisha kuthibitishwa kisheria, hakuna awezaye kuubatilisha wala kuuongezea masharti mapya.
sw.R: Ndugu, huu ni mfano kutoka katika maisha ya kila siku. Mtu akiandika wosia na ukisha kuthibitishwa rasmi, hakuna anayeweza kuufuta au kuuongezea kitu.

fr.L: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, je parle en termes humains : même une alliance humaine, une fois ratifiée, personne ne l’annule ni n’y ajoute.
fr.B: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, je vais prendre un exemple dans la vie de tous les jours. Prenez un testament : une fois qu’il est devenu valide, personne ne peut l’annuler ni y ajouter de nouvelles clauses, et pourtant ce n’est qu’un acte humain.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, voici un exemple tiré de la vie de tous les jours. Quand quelqu’un fait un testament et que ce testament est devenu officiel, personne ne peut l’annuler ni rien y ajouter.

decisions.choice: I speak in human terms: an illustration drawn from everyday human dealings
alternatives: I speak as a mere man would, without authority
decisions.reason: The phrase introduces a comparison from ordinary life, as in Romans 3:5 and 6:19. Paul is not lowering his authority; he is arguing from how people treat a binding document to how God treats his own promise.

decisions.choice: a will, the everyday sense of the word, chosen because the same word is the Scriptures' word for God's covenant
alternatives: a covenant or agreement between people
decisions.reason: διαθήκη was the ordinary Greek word for a will or testament, a binding arrangement made by one person about what others will receive. The Greek Scriptures use the same word for God's covenant with Abraham, and Paul uses it in that sense in verse 17, where it is "ratified beforehand by God". The talk of inheritance (verse 18) and heirs (verse 29) fits a will. But a will could normally be changed by the one who made it, so some read the word here as a human agreement or covenant, which neither party may change alone. Either way the point is the same: once in force it stands.

decisions.choice: sets aside or adds to: annul it or add new terms to it
decisions.reason: ἀθετέω means to declare void. ἐπιδιατάσσομαι, found only here in the New Testament, means to add further provisions. Paul has in view the law of Moses, which in his argument would be such an added provision if it changed the terms of the promise (verse 17).

decisions.choice: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}
decisions.reason: Paul writes to the churches of Galatia, women and men, and in verse 28 says that in Christ there is "male and female" alike. "Brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: covenant (L); will (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word that verse 17 needs, so the reader can see that it is the same word. Balanced and Readable use the sense that the illustration has in ordinary life (meaning note m2), and verse 17 returns to "covenant" for God's arrangement with Abraham; the footnote tells the reader that one Greek word stands behind both.

decisions.choice: I will use an illustration from human life (B); here is an example from ordinary life (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek idiom says what kind of argument follows; Balanced and Readable say so in plain words.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in Romans and Philippians 4:1, Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so the Spanish has no gender setting here or elsewhere in the chapter.

decisions.choice: pacto (L); testamento (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "pacto", the word verse 17 uses for God's covenant. Balanced and Readable use "testamento", a will, the sense the illustration has in ordinary life (meaning note m2). Spanish "testamento" is also the old word for God's covenant ("Antiguo Testamento"), so the link the footnote explains is still audible.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: Swahili "ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so the Swahili has no gender setting here or elsewhere in the chapter.

decisions.choice: alliance (L); testament (B, R) in 3:15; alliance at every level in 3:17
decisions.reason: As in Hebrews 9:16-17, French has the two words the English has: Literal keeps "alliance", the word verse 17 needs, and Balanced and Readable use "testament", the everyday sense the illustration has (m2). The French "testament" also echoes the "Ancien" and "Nouveau Testament", which suits Paul's play on the one Greek word.

source.text: τῷ δὲ Ἀβραὰμ ἐρρέθησαν αἱ ἐπαγγελίαι καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ· οὐ λέγει· Καὶ τοῖς σπέρμασιν, ὡς ἐπὶ πολλῶν, ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐφ’ ἑνός· Καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου, ὅς ἐστιν Χριστός.

records.literal_gloss: And to Abraham were spoken the promises and to the seed of him. Not it says, And to the seeds, as of many, but as of one, And to the seed of you, who is Christ.

en.L: Now to Abraham the promises were spoken, and to his seed. It does not say, "And to the seeds," as [referring] to many, but as [referring] to one, "And to your seed," who is {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his descendant. Notice that Scripture does not say "and to descendants," as if many people were meant. It speaks of one: "and to your descendant," and that one is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: God spoke the promises to Abraham and to his descendant. Scripture does not say "descendants," as if it were talking about many people. It says "your descendant," which means one person, and that person is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

es.L: Ahora bien, a Abraham le fueron dichas las promesas, y a su simiente. No dice: «Y a las simientes», como [refiriéndose] a muchos, sino como [refiriéndose] a uno: «Y a tu simiente», que es {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}.
es.B: Las promesas se le dijeron a Abraham y a su descendiente. {{plural_you:Fíjense|Fijaos}} en que la Escritura no dice «y a los descendientes», como si se tratara de muchos. Habla de uno solo: «y a tu descendiente», y ese uno es {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.
es.R: Dios le hizo las promesas a Abraham y a su descendiente. La Escritura no dice «descendientes», como si hablara de muchas personas. Dice «tu descendiente», es decir, una sola persona, y esa persona es {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.

sw.L: Basi kwa Ibrahimu ahadi zilinenwa, na kwa mzao wake. Haisemi, "Na kwa wazao," kana kwamba [inawahusu] wengi, bali kana kwamba [inamhusu] mmoja, "Na kwa mzao wako," ambaye ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Ahadi zilitamkwa kwa Ibrahimu na kwa mzao wake. Angalieni kwamba Maandiko hayasemi "na kwa wazao," kana kwamba watu wengi walikusudiwa. Yanazungumza juu ya mmoja: "na kwa mzao wako," na huyo mmoja ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Mungu alimpa Ibrahimu ahadi, yeye na mzao wake. Maandiko hayasemi "wazao," kana kwamba yanazungumza juu ya watu wengi. Yanasema "mzao wako," yaani mtu mmoja, na mtu huyo ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

fr.L: Or c’est à Abraham que les promesses ont été dites, et à sa descendance. Il ne dit pas : « et aux descendances », comme [s’il s’agissait] de plusieurs, mais comme d’une seule : « et à ta descendance », qui est {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.B: Les promesses ont été faites à Abraham et à son descendant. Remarquez que l’Écriture ne dit pas « et à tes descendants », comme s’il s’agissait de beaucoup de gens. Elle parle d’un seul : « et à ton descendant », et ce descendant, c’est le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Dieu a fait les promesses à Abraham et à son descendant. L’Écriture ne dit pas « tes descendants », comme si elle parlait de beaucoup de gens. Elle dit « ton descendant », ce qui veut dire une seule personne, et cette personne, c’est le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

decisions.choice: "and to your seed": the promise to Abraham in Genesis
alternatives: a quotation of one verse only
decisions.reason: The words come from God's promises to Abraham, repeated several times: Genesis 13:15, 17:8 and 24:7 (compare 12:7 and 22:18). That is why Paul speaks of "the promises" in the plural. The land and the blessing were promised both to Abraham and to his descendants.

decisions.choice: the singular "seed" points to one descendant, Christ, in whom all his people are included
alternatives: Paul denies that the word can mean many descendants
a play on words with no real argument
decisions.reason: σπέρμα is a collective noun: in Genesis it means all of Abraham's descendants, and Paul knows this, for in verse 29 he calls the Galatian believers Abraham's "seed". His point is that the promise always looked to one line, and in the end to one person, the Messiah, through whom the blessing reaches the nations (3:14). Those who belong to Christ are counted as the seed because they are in him (verse 29). The plural σπέρμασιν is an unusual form, used here to make the contrast.

decisions.choice: it says: Scripture, through which God speaks
alternatives: he says, with God as the subject
decisions.reason: λέγω has no stated subject. In 3:8 Paul speaks of Scripture foreseeing and announcing, and in 3:22 of Scripture shutting up all things; the subject here is Scripture or God speaking in it, which comes to the same.

decisions.choice: seed (L); descendant (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Seed" keeps the old picture and the singular form of the Greek. In modern English it is rarely used for people, so Balanced and Readable use a plain word for a person's children and their line. Here they need one that has a separate singular and plural (r-en-5).

decisions.choice: Scripture
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject the Greek leaves understood (meaning note m3).

decisions.choice: God spoke the promises
decisions.reason: Readable turns the passive into an active verb and names God, who made the promises.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting: "Christ" by default, "Messiah" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: descendant / descendants
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Balanced and Readable say "offspring", but in English that word is the same in the singular and the plural, so it cannot show the contrast Paul draws here between one and many. "Descendant" and "descendants" can.

decisions.choice: simiente (L); descendiente / descendientes (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Descendencia", the usual Spanish word for a person's offspring, is collective and cannot show the contrast Paul draws between one and many. "Descendiente" and "descendientes" can. Literal keeps "simiente", the old Spanish word for seed used of people, which has a plural.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Fíjense|Fijaos}}
decisions.reason: English "Notice" addresses the readers; Spanish has to choose a plural imperative, so it is a reader setting (ustedes form first, vosotros form second), as every plural "you" in Paul's letters is.

decisions.choice: mzao / wazao (every level)
decisions.reason: Swahili "uzao", which Literal uses for seed elsewhere (Romans 9:7), is collective and has no plural, so it cannot show the contrast between one and many. "Mzao" (one descendant) and "wazao" (descendants), from the same root "-zaa", can, and are used at every level here and in verse 19. A reviewer may judge "mzao" too rare at Literal.

decisions.choice: descendance, descendances (L); descendant, descendants (B, R); the same in 3:19; "la descendance d'Abraham" (L, B) and "les descendants d'Abraham" (R) in 3:29
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a collective singular, like "descendance", which Literal uses so that the singular and the odd plural show Paul's contrast between one and many (m2). "Semence" is no longer said of people. Balanced and Readable say "descendant", one person, as the English does; in 3:29 the many believers together are Abraham's "descendance".

source.text: τοῦτο δὲ λέγω· διαθήκην προκεκυρωμένην ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ μετὰ τετρακόσια καὶ τριάκοντα ἔτη γεγονὼς νόμος οὐκ ἀκυροῖ, εἰς τὸ καταργῆσαι τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν.

records.literal_gloss: This and I say: covenant having been ratified beforehand by the God, the after four hundred and thirty years having come law not annuls, so as to nullify the promise.

en.L: And this I say: a covenant ratified beforehand by God, the law that came 430 years afterward does not annul, so as to make the promise void.
en.B: My point is this. God had already ratified a covenant, and the law, coming 430 years afterward, cannot overturn it and so cancel the promise.
en.R: This is what I mean. God made a covenant with Abraham and made it binding. The law came 430 years later. It cannot cancel that covenant and so do away with what God promised.

es.L: Y esto digo: un pacto ratificado de antemano por Dios, la ley que vino 430 años después no [lo] anula, como para invalidar la promesa.
es.B: Lo que quiero decir es esto: Dios ya había ratificado un pacto, y la ley, que llegó 430 años después, no puede anularlo y dejar así sin efecto la promesa.
es.R: Esto es lo que quiero decir. Dios hizo un pacto con Abraham y lo dejó firme. La ley llegó 430 años más tarde. No puede anular ese pacto ni acabar con lo que Dios prometió.

sw.L: Na hili nasema: agano lililothibitishwa kabla na Mungu, sheria iliyokuja miaka mia nne na thelathini baadaye hailitangui, hata kuifanya ahadi kuwa batili.
sw.B: Ninachomaanisha ni hiki: Mungu alikuwa amekwisha kulithibitisha agano, na sheria, iliyokuja miaka mia nne na thelathini baadaye, haiwezi kulitangua na hivyo kuibatilisha ahadi.
sw.R: Hivi ndivyo ninavyomaanisha. Mungu alifanya agano na Ibrahimu, akalithibitisha. Sheria ilikuja miaka mia nne na thelathini baadaye. Haiwezi kulifuta agano hilo na hivyo kuondoa kile ambacho Mungu aliahidi.

fr.L: Voici ce que je dis : une alliance ratifiée d’avance par Dieu, la Loi venue 430 ans après ne l’annule pas, de manière à rendre la promesse sans effet.
fr.B: Voici où je veux en venir. Dieu avait déjà ratifié une alliance, et la Loi, venue 430 ans plus tard, ne peut pas l’annuler et rendre ainsi la promesse sans effet.
fr.R: Voici ce que je veux dire. Dieu a fait une alliance avec Abraham et l’a rendue valide. La Loi est venue 430 ans plus tard. Elle ne peut pas annuler cette alliance, ni supprimer ainsi ce que Dieu avait promis.

decisions.choice: God's covenant with Abraham, already made binding before the law
decisions.reason: The same word as in verse 15 now names God's own arrangement with Abraham (Genesis 15:18; 17:1-8). The prefix in προκυρόω means "ratified beforehand": it was in force long before Sinai.

decisions.choice: 430 years: the period Exodus gives for Israel's stay before the exodus
alternatives: an exact count from Abraham to Sinai
decisions.reason: Exodus 12:40-41 gives 430 years for Israel's time in Egypt; the Greek Old Testament counts the same 430 years for the time in Canaan and Egypt together. Genesis 15:13 and Acts 7:6 round it to 400. Paul uses the familiar figure to say the law came long after the promise.

decisions.choice: so as to make the promise void: what annulling the covenant would amount to
alternatives: the law's purpose was to cancel the promise
decisions.reason: The construction gives the result that would follow if the law annulled the covenant. Paul denies both: the law does not annul the covenant, so it does not make the promise void.
Numbers above ninety-nine are written in figures.

decisions.choice: a covenant with Abraham
decisions.reason: Readable names the other party, whom verses 16 and 18 name, so the reader knows which covenant is meant.

decisions.choice: a covenant ... the law ... does not annul
alternatives: the law does not annul a covenant
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order, which puts the covenant first for emphasis.

decisions.choice: miaka mia nne na thelathini
decisions.reason: Swahili running text writes numbers in words (docs/swahili-style.md, section 4), where English uses figures for numbers above ninety-nine.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ ἐκ νόμου ἡ κληρονομία, οὐκέτι ἐξ ἐπαγγελίας· τῷ δὲ Ἀβραὰμ δι’ ἐπαγγελίας κεχάρισται ὁ θεός.

records.literal_gloss: If for from law the inheritance, no longer from promise; but to Abraham through promise has granted the God.

en.L: For if the inheritance [is] from [the] law, [it is] no longer from promise; but to Abraham God has freely given [it] through promise.
en.B: For if the inheritance depends on the law, it no longer depends on a promise. But God gave it freely to Abraham by means of a promise.
en.R: If the inheritance came from keeping the law, it would no longer come from a promise. But God gave it to Abraham as a gift, by promising it.

es.L: Porque si la herencia [es] por [la] ley, ya no [es] por promesa; pero a Abraham Dios [se la] ha concedido gratuitamente por medio de promesa.
es.B: Porque si la herencia depende de la ley, ya no depende de una promesa. Pero Dios se la concedió gratuitamente a Abraham por medio de una promesa.
es.R: Si la herencia viniera por cumplir la ley, ya no vendría por una promesa. Pero Dios se la regaló a Abraham al prometérsela.

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa urithi [ni] kwa sheria, [si] kwa ahadi tena; lakini Mungu amemkirimia Ibrahimu [urithi] kwa njia ya ahadi.
sw.B: Kwa maana ikiwa urithi unategemea sheria, hautegemei tena ahadi. Lakini Mungu alimkirimia Ibrahimu urithi huo kwa njia ya ahadi.
sw.R: Kama urithi ungetokana na kushika sheria, usingetokana tena na ahadi. Lakini Mungu alimpa Ibrahimu urithi huo kama zawadi, kwa kumwahidi.

fr.L: Car si l’héritage [vient] de la Loi, il ne [vient] plus de la promesse ; mais à Abraham, Dieu [l’]a accordé par grâce au moyen d’une promesse.
fr.B: Car si l’héritage dépend de la Loi, il ne dépend plus d’une promesse. Or Dieu l’a donné gratuitement à Abraham par le moyen d’une promesse.
fr.R: Si l’héritage venait de l’obéissance à la Loi, il ne viendrait plus d’une promesse. Mais Dieu l’a donné à Abraham comme un cadeau, en le lui promettant.

decisions.choice: the inheritance: what God promised to give Abraham and his offspring
decisions.reason: In Genesis the inheritance was the land (Genesis 15:7; 17:8). In Galatians Paul widens it to all that God promised: the blessing of Abraham and the Spirit (3:14), sonship (4:7) and the kingdom of God (5:21).

decisions.choice: from law, from promise: the law and the promise as two different grounds
alternatives: the inheritance can rest on both together
decisions.reason: Paul sets the two against each other: if the inheritance depends on keeping the law, it no longer rests on a promise, because a promise is kept by the one who makes it, while the law depends on what people do (3:12).

decisions.choice: has given freely, as a gift, and the gift still stands
alternatives: has granted as a right earned
decisions.reason: χαρίζομαι comes from the same root as the word for grace: it means to give as a favor. The perfect tense says that the gift given to Abraham remains in force.

decisions.choice: from keeping the law
decisions.reason: Readable says how the inheritance would come from the law: by doing what it commands.

decisions.choice: freely given (L); gave it freely (B); gave it ... as a gift (R)
decisions.reason: "Granted" loses the note of free favor in the Greek verb (meaning note m3).

decisions.choice: amemkirimia (L); alimkirimia (B); alimpa ... kama zawadi (R)
decisions.reason: "Kukirimia" is to give generously, as a favor (meaning note m3). "Kumpa bure" would say "free of charge", but "bure" also means "in vain", which would mislead here.

decisions.choice: accordé par grâce (L); donné gratuitement (B); comme un cadeau (R)
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the root of "grace" and means to give as a favor (m3). Literal keeps the link with "grâce".

en.B: What, then, was the law for?
en.R: Then what was the purpose of the law?

es.R: Entonces, ¿cuál era el propósito de la ley?

sw.B: Basi, sheria ilikuwa ya kazi gani?
sw.R: Basi, sheria ilikuwa na kusudi gani?

fr.B: À quoi servait donc la Loi ?
fr.R: Alors, quel était le but de la Loi ?

decisions.choice: why the law: what was its purpose
decisions.reason: The question has no verb. After verses 15-18 have shown that the law cannot add to or cancel the promise, the natural question is what it was for, and the answer that follows gives its purpose and its time limit.

decisions.choice: was ... for (B); was the purpose of (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb the Greek leaves out and make the question a question about purpose.

source.text: τῶν παραβάσεων χάριν προσετέθη, ἄχρις οὗ ἔλθῃ τὸ σπέρμα ᾧ ἐπήγγελται, διαταγεὶς δι’ ἀγγέλων ἐν χειρὶ μεσίτου·

records.literal_gloss: Of the transgressions because of it was added, until should come the seed to whom it has been promised, having been ordered through angels by hand of a mediator.

en.L: It was added for the sake of transgressions, until the seed would come to whom [the promise] has been made, being ordered through angels by [the] hand of a mediator.
en.B: It was added because of transgressions, and only until the offspring should come, the one to whom the promise was made. Angels set it in order, and it came through the hand of a mediator.
en.R: It was added because of wrongdoing, and it was meant to last only until the offspring came, the one God's promise was about. God gave the law through angels, and it was handed on by a go-between, Moses.

es.L: Fue añadida a causa de las transgresiones, hasta que viniera la simiente a quien [la promesa] ha sido hecha, siendo ordenada por medio de ángeles por mano de un mediador.
es.B: Fue añadida a causa de las transgresiones, y solo hasta que viniera el descendiente, aquel a quien se hizo la promesa. Unos ángeles la pusieron en orden, y llegó por mano de un mediador.
es.R: Se añadió a causa de las faltas de la gente, y debía durar solo hasta que viniera el descendiente del que hablaba la promesa de Dios. Dios dio la ley por medio de ángeles, y la entregó un intermediario, Moisés.

sw.L: Iliongezwa kwa ajili ya uvunjaji wa amri, mpaka aje yule mzao ambaye [ahadi] imetolewa kwake, ikiwa imepangwa kupitia malaika kwa mkono wa mpatanishi.
sw.B: Iliongezwa kwa sababu ya uvunjaji wa amri, na kwa muda tu, mpaka aje yule mzao, yule ambaye ahadi ilitolewa kwake. Malaika waliipanga, nayo ikaja kwa mkono wa mpatanishi.
sw.R: Iliongezwa kwa sababu ya makosa ya watu, na ilikusudiwa kudumu mpaka aje yule mzao ambaye ahadi ya Mungu ilimhusu. Mungu aliitoa sheria kupitia malaika, nayo ikakabidhiwa watu na mtu wa kati, yaani Musa.

fr.L: Elle a été ajoutée à cause des transgressions, jusqu’à ce que vienne la descendance à qui [la promesse] a été faite, ayant été promulguée par des anges, par la main d’un médiateur.
fr.B: Elle a été ajoutée à cause des transgressions, et seulement jusqu’à la venue du descendant à qui la promesse avait été faite. Des anges l’ont mise en ordre, et elle est venue par la main d’un médiateur.
fr.R: Elle a été ajoutée à cause des fautes des gens, et elle ne devait durer que jusqu’à la venue du descendant dont parlait la promesse de Dieu. Dieu a donné la Loi par des anges, et elle a été transmise par un intermédiaire, Moïse.

decisions.choice: because of transgressions: to bring them to light as the breaking of a clear command
alternatives: to hold back sin until Christ came
decisions.reason: χάριν after a noun means "for the sake of" or "because of" and does not say how. παράβασις is the stepping over of a known command. Romans 4:15 and 5:20 suggest that the law made wrongdoing visible as transgression; the picture of the guardian in verses 23-24 suggests that it also held sin in check. The text leaves both possible.

decisions.choice: until the offspring came: the law was given for a limited time
alternatives: until the end of the world
decisions.reason: The law had a beginning (430 years after the promise, verse 17) and an end, the coming of the one offspring, Christ (verse 16). Verses 23-25 make the same point with the picture of the guardian.

decisions.choice: angels and a mediator: the giving of the law at Sinai through angels and Moses
decisions.reason: Jewish tradition held that angels were present when the law was given (Deuteronomy 33:2 in the Greek Old Testament; Acts 7:38, 53; Hebrews 2:2). The mediator is Moses, who stood between the Lord and the people (Deuteronomy 5:5). Paul's point is that the law came at one remove, while the promise was spoken by God himself (verse 18).

decisions.choice: seed (L); offspring (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 16.

decisions.choice: God's promise; God gave the law; Moses
alternatives: the promise was made; it was ordered; a mediator
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who promised and gave the law, and the mediator, whom meaning note m3 identifies.

decisions.choice: wrongdoing
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word; Literal and Balanced keep "transgressions", the breaking of a command.

decisions.choice: uvunjaji wa amri (L, B); makosa ya watu (R)
decisions.reason: Romans uses "kosa" for a different Greek word, a false step. The word here is the stepping over of a known command (meaning note m1), so Literal and Balanced say "the breaking of commands"; Readable uses the common word, as the English does.

source.text: ὁ δὲ μεσίτης ἑνὸς οὐκ ἔστιν, ὁ δὲ θεὸς εἷς ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: The but mediator of one not is, the but God one is.

en.L: Now the mediator is not of one, but God is one.
en.B: Now a mediator does not act for one party alone, but God is one.
en.R: A go-between always stands between two sides, but God is one.

es.L: Ahora bien, el mediador no es de uno [solo], pero Dios es uno.
es.B: Ahora bien, un mediador no actúa en nombre de una sola parte, pero Dios es uno.
es.R: Un intermediario siempre está entre dos partes, pero Dios es uno solo.

sw.L: Basi mpatanishi si wa mmoja, lakini Mungu ni mmoja.
sw.B: Basi mpatanishi hafanyi kazi kwa ajili ya upande mmoja peke yake, lakini Mungu ni mmoja.
sw.R: Mtu wa kati husimama kati ya pande mbili, lakini Mungu ni mmoja.

fr.L: Or le médiateur n’est pas d’un seul, mais Dieu est un.
fr.B: Or un médiateur n’agit pas pour une seule partie, mais Dieu est un.
fr.R: Un intermédiaire se tient toujours entre deux parties, mais Dieu est un.

decisions.choice: a mediator stands between parties, but the promise came straight from the one God
alternatives: God is one, so the law and the promise cannot conflict
the one God is the God of Jews and Gentiles alike (Romans 3:29-30)
decisions.reason: This is one of the hardest sentences in Paul's letters, and it has been read in very many ways. The reading followed here takes it with verse 19: the law came through a go-between, which implies two parties, God and Israel, with angels between; the promise was given to Abraham directly by God, who is one and acts alone.

decisions.choice: God is one: an echo of the Shema
decisions.reason: "God is one" recalls the confession of Israel in Deuteronomy 6:4. Paul uses the same words in Romans 3:30.

decisions.choice: does not act for one party alone (B); stands between two sides (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is compressed; Balanced and Readable say what "not of one" means about a mediator.

source.text: Ὁ οὖν νόμος κατὰ τῶν ἐπαγγελιῶν τοῦ θεοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: The then law against the promises of the God?

en.L: [Is] the law then against the promises of God?
en.B: Does the law, then, oppose God's promises?
en.R: Does this mean that the law is against God's promises?

es.L: ¿[Es] la ley, pues, contraria a las promesas de Dios?
es.B: ¿Se opone, entonces, la ley a las promesas de Dios?
es.R: ¿Quiere decir esto que la ley está en contra de las promesas de Dios?

sw.L: Je, basi sheria [iko] kinyume cha ahadi za Mungu?
sw.B: Je, basi sheria inapingana na ahadi za Mungu?
sw.R: Je, hii inamaanisha kwamba sheria iko kinyume na ahadi za Mungu?

fr.L: La Loi [est-elle] donc contre les promesses de Dieu ?
fr.B: La Loi s’oppose-t-elle donc aux promesses de Dieu ?
fr.R: Est-ce que cela veut dire que la Loi est contre les promesses de Dieu ?

decisions.choice: of God: read
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, among them the oldest papyrus of Paul's letters and Codex Vaticanus, leave out "of God". The SBLGNT keeps the words, and the sense is the same either way: the promises are God's.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer "no"
decisions.reason: If the law was added later and came through a go-between, a reader might think it works against the promise. Paul raises the objection in order to reject it.

source.text: μὴ γένοιτο· εἰ γὰρ ἐδόθη νόμος ὁ δυνάμενος ζῳοποιῆσαι, ὄντως ἐκ νόμου ἂν ἦν ἡ δικαιοσύνη.

records.literal_gloss: Not may it be! If for was given law the being able to make alive, really from law would have been the righteousness.

en.L: May it not be! For if a law had been given that was able to give life, righteousness would truly have been from [the] law.
en.B: Certainly not! Had any law been given with the power to make people alive, then righteousness would in fact come by way of the law.
en.R: Of course not! If God had given a law that had the power to give life, then righteousness really would come from keeping the law.

es.L: ¡No sea así! Porque si se hubiera dado una ley capaz de dar vida, verdaderamente la justicia habría sido por [la] ley.
es.B: ¡De ningún modo! Si se hubiera dado una ley con poder para dar vida, entonces la justicia vendría de verdad por medio de la ley.
es.R: ¡Claro que no! Si Dios hubiera dado una ley con poder para dar vida, entonces la justicia vendría de verdad por cumplir la ley.

sw.L: Isiwe hivyo! Kwa maana kama ingetolewa sheria yenye uwezo wa kuhuisha, kwa kweli haki ingetokana na sheria.
sw.B: Hasha! Kama sheria yoyote ingetolewa yenye nguvu ya kuwapa watu uzima, basi haki ingepatikana kweli kwa njia ya sheria.
sw.R: Sivyo kabisa! Kama Mungu angetoa sheria yenye nguvu ya kuwapa watu uzima, basi haki ingepatikana kweli kwa kushika sheria.

fr.L: Qu’il n’en soit rien ! Car si une loi avait été donnée qui soit capable de faire vivre, la justice viendrait réellement de la loi.
fr.B: Absolument pas ! Si une loi avait été donnée avec le pouvoir de faire vivre, alors la justice viendrait vraiment de la loi.
fr.R: Pas du tout ! Si Dieu avait donné une loi capable de donner la vie, alors on deviendrait vraiment juste devant Dieu en obéissant à cette loi.

decisions.choice: a strong rejection: certainly not
alternatives: a wish: may it not happen
decisions.reason: μὴ γένοιτο is Paul's usual way of rejecting a wrong conclusion (2:17; Romans 3:4, 6:2).

decisions.choice: give life: the life God gives, which the law cannot give
decisions.reason: ζῳοποιέω is giving life to the dead (Romans 4:17; 8:11). Paul has quoted "the righteous will live by faith" (3:11); the law can command but cannot give that life. Compare 2 Corinthians 3:6, "the Spirit gives life".

decisions.choice: righteousness: being in the right before God
decisions.reason: As in 2:21, righteousness is the standing God gives, the result of being justified (verse 24). If the law could give life, it could give this standing too; but it cannot.

decisions.choice: If God had given; from keeping the law
alternatives: if a law had been given; from the law
decisions.reason: Readable names the giver and says how righteousness would come from the law.

decisions.choice: May it not be! (L); Certainly not! (B); Of course not! (R)
decisions.reason: Each level gives the force of the strong rejection in its own register; "God forbid" adds a name the Greek does not have.

decisions.choice: une loi ... la loi, lowercase
decisions.reason: Paul speaks of any law that could give life, not of the law of Moses by name, so French writes it without the capital used elsewhere in the letter.

source.text: ἀλλὰ συνέκλεισεν ἡ γραφὴ τὰ πάντα ὑπὸ ἁμαρτίαν ἵνα ἡ ἐπαγγελία ἐκ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοθῇ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: But shut up the Scripture the all things under sin, so that the promise from faith of Jesus Christ might be given to the ones believing.

en.L: But the Scripture shut up all things under sin, so that the promise, from faith in Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, might be given to those who believe.
en.B: But Scripture has locked up everything under the power of sin, so that what was promised might be given, on the ground of faith in Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, to those who believe.
en.R: But Scripture has shut up everyone and everything as prisoners under sin. It did this so that the promise would be given, through faith in Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, to those who believe.

es.L: Pero la Escritura encerró todas las cosas bajo pecado, para que la promesa, por fe en {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, fuese dada a los que creen.
es.B: Pero la Escritura ha encerrado todo bajo el poder del pecado, para que lo prometido se diera, sobre la base de la fe en {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, a los que creen.
es.R: Pero la Escritura ha encerrado a todos y todo como prisioneros bajo el pecado. Lo hizo para que la promesa se diera, por medio de la fe en {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, a los que creen.

sw.L: Lakini Maandiko yalivifunga vitu vyote chini ya dhambi, ili ahadi, kwa imani katika Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, itolewe kwa wale wanaoamini.
sw.B: Lakini Maandiko yamevifunga vitu vyote chini ya utawala wa dhambi, ili kile kilichoahidiwa kitolewe kwa wale wanaoamini, kwa msingi wa imani katika Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Lakini Maandiko yamewafunga watu wote na kila kitu kama wafungwa chini ya dhambi. Yalifanya hivyo ili ahadi itolewe kwa wale wanaoamini, kupitia imani katika Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

fr.L: Mais l’Écriture a tout enfermé sous le péché, afin que la promesse soit donnée, par la foi en Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, à ceux qui croient.
fr.B: Mais l’Écriture a enfermé toutes choses sous le pouvoir du péché, pour que ce qui avait été promis soit donné, sur la base de la foi en Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, à ceux qui croient.
fr.R: Mais l’Écriture a enfermé tout le monde et toutes choses comme des prisonniers sous le péché. Elle l’a fait pour que la promesse soit donnée à ceux qui croient, par la foi en Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

decisions.choice: Scripture declared all people prisoners of sin
decisions.reason: Paul speaks of Scripture acting, as in 3:8, because what Scripture says is God's verdict. Passages such as Deuteronomy 27:26, quoted in 3:10, and those gathered in Romans 3:10-18 declare everyone guilty. Romans 11:32 uses the same verb of God: he has shut up all in disobedience, so that he may have mercy on all.

decisions.choice: all things: the whole human race and its world
decisions.reason: The neuter "all things" is all-inclusive. Paul means Jews and Gentiles alike, as in Romans 3:9, "all are under sin".

decisions.choice: faith in Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: With a person's name after it, πίστις can mean faith that person has or faith directed to that person. Read the second way, Paul means the believer's faith in Jesus Christ. Read the first way, he means Christ's own faithfulness to God, shown in his obedience to the cross, and "those who believe" at the end of the verse is the human answer to it. For "faith in Christ": the same verse goes on to speak of believing, and in 2:16 the same kind of phrase sits beside "we too have believed in Christ Jesus". For "faithfulness of Christ": the verse would otherwise name the believer's faith twice, and verses 23 and 25 speak of faith "coming" as an event in history, which suits Christ's own faithfulness. Both readings agree that the promise is given through Christ and not through the law. We follow the first and give the second in a footnote, as in Philippians 3:9.

decisions.choice: under the power of sin (B); as prisoners under sin (R)
decisions.reason: "Under sin" means under sin's rule (Romans 3:9; 7:14); Balanced says so, and Readable keeps the picture of the verb, shutting in like prisoners.

decisions.choice: what was promised
decisions.reason: The promise here is what was promised, the gift itself (3:14), which is given to believers.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting: "Christ" by default, "Messiah" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: Spanish joins the name and the title in "Jesucristo", so the title setting replaces the whole name: "Jesús, el Mesías".

source.text: Πρὸ τοῦ δὲ ἐλθεῖν τὴν πίστιν ὑπὸ νόμον ἐφρουρούμεθα συγκλειόμενοι εἰς τὴν μέλλουσαν πίστιν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι.

records.literal_gloss: Before the and to come the faith, under law we were being guarded, being shut up for the being about faith to be revealed.

en.L: Now before the faith came, we were kept under guard under [the] law, being shut up for the faith that was about to be revealed.
en.B: Until faith came, the law held us in custody. We were kept shut in, waiting for the faith that was going to be revealed.
en.R: Before the time of faith came, the law kept us under guard like prisoners. We were shut in until the faith that was coming would be made known.

es.L: Pero antes de que viniera la fe, estábamos custodiados bajo [la] ley, encerrados para la fe que había de ser revelada.
es.B: Antes de que llegara la fe, la ley nos tenía bajo custodia. Estábamos encerrados, esperando la fe que iba a ser revelada.
es.R: Antes de que llegara el tiempo de la fe, la ley nos vigilaba como a prisioneros. Estábamos encerrados hasta que se diera a conocer la fe que había de venir.

sw.L: Lakini kabla ya ile imani kuja, tulikuwa tukilindwa chini ya sheria, tukiwa tumefungiwa kwa ajili ya ile imani iliyokuwa karibu kufunuliwa.
sw.B: Kabla imani haijaja, sheria ilitushika chini ya ulinzi. Tulikuwa tumefungiwa, tukiingojea ile imani ambayo ingefunuliwa.
sw.R: Kabla wakati wa imani haujafika, sheria ilitulinda kama wafungwa. Tulikuwa tumefungiwa mpaka imani ile iliyokuwa inakuja ijulikane.

fr.L: Or, avant que vienne la foi, nous étions gardés sous la Loi, enfermés en vue de la foi qui devait être révélée.
fr.B: Avant que la foi vienne, la Loi nous tenait sous bonne garde. Nous étions enfermés, dans l’attente de la foi qui allait être révélée.
fr.R: Avant que vienne le temps de la foi, la Loi nous gardait comme des prisonniers. Nous étions enfermés jusqu’à ce que la foi qui devait venir soit connue.

decisions.choice: the faith: faith in Christ as a new stage in God's plan, which came and was revealed
alternatives: the Christian faith as a body of teaching
decisions.reason: Abraham believed long before (3:6), so Paul does not mean that no one had faith before Christ. With the article he speaks of faith as something that "came" and "was revealed" at a set time, when Christ came (verses 24-25; 4:4). Faith here stands for the new way God deals with people in Christ.

decisions.choice: kept under guard: held in custody, guarded and confined
decisions.reason: φρουρέω is used of guarding a city or keeping watch over prisoners (2 Corinthians 11:32); συγκλείω repeats the "shutting up" of verse 22. The picture is mainly of confinement, but the next verse's guardian shows that the custody had a good purpose and an end.

decisions.choice: we: Paul and his fellow Jews, who lived under the law
decisions.reason: "Under the law" fits Israel first. But in 4:3-9 Paul says that Gentiles too were enslaved before Christ, and in 3:26 he moves to "you all", so the "we" may already include them.

decisions.choice: the law held us in custody (B); the law kept us under guard (R)
alternatives: we were held in custody under the law
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the law the subject of an active verb, which reads more plainly in English.

decisions.choice: the time of faith
decisions.reason: Readable says that the coming of faith is a time in God's plan (meaning note m1).

source.text: ὥστε ὁ νόμος παιδαγωγὸς ἡμῶν γέγονεν εἰς Χριστόν, ἵνα ἐκ πίστεως δικαιωθῶμεν·

records.literal_gloss: So that the law guardian of us has become unto Christ, so that from faith we might be justified.

en.L: So the law has become our guardian until {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, so that we might be justified by faith.
en.B: In this way the law served as our guardian until the coming of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, so that faith would be the way we are justified.
en.R: So the law was like a guardian, the servant who was put in charge of a child, until {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} came. Then we could be put right with God by faith.

es.L: De manera que la ley ha llegado a ser nuestro guía hasta {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, para que fuésemos justificados por fe.
es.B: Así, la ley fue nuestro guía hasta la venida {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, para que la fe fuera el camino por el cual somos justificados.
es.R: Así que la ley era como un guía, el siervo encargado de cuidar a un niño, hasta que {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} vino. Entonces Dios pudo declararnos justos por la fe.

sw.L: Hivyo sheria imekuwa mlezi wetu mpaka {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ili tuhesabiwe haki kwa imani.
sw.B: Kwa njia hii sheria ilikuwa mlezi wetu mpaka kuja kwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ili imani iwe njia ya sisi kuhesabiwa haki.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo sheria ilikuwa kama mlezi, yule mtumishi aliyewekwa kumtunza mtoto, mpaka {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alipokuja. Kisha tukaweza kuhesabiwa haki na Mungu kwa imani.

fr.L: Ainsi la Loi a été notre gardien jusqu’au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, afin que nous soyons justifiés par la foi.
fr.B: Ainsi, la Loi a été notre gardien jusqu’à la venue du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, pour que ce soit par la foi que nous soyons justifiés.
fr.R: La Loi était donc comme un gardien, le serviteur chargé de surveiller un enfant, jusqu’à ce que le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} vienne. Alors nous pouvions être déclarés justes par Dieu grâce à la foi.

decisions.choice: guardian: the household slave who watched over a boy until he came of age
alternatives: a schoolmaster or tutor who taught him
decisions.reason: In Greek and Roman homes the παιδαγωγός was a slave who looked after a boy from early childhood until his teens: he took him to school, kept him from trouble and corrected him. He was not the teacher. Paul's point is that the law had charge of God's people for a limited time, like a child who is not yet an heir in full (4:1-2).

decisions.choice: until Christ: the guardian's time lasted until Christ came
decisions.reason: εἰς can mean "until" or "to, leading to". Verses 23 and 25 are about time, before faith came and after, so "until Christ" fits the passage best. The older reading, that the law led people to Christ, is true to what Paul says elsewhere of the law, but does not seem to be his point here.

decisions.choice: justified: declared by God to be in the right before him, acquitted and accepted
alternatives: treated as if righteous with no real change of standing
decisions.reason: δικαιόω is a law-court word: the judge declares someone in the right. In Galatians God is the judge, and those he justifies are acquitted and accepted as his own (2:16; 3:8, 11). The life of the Spirit follows from this, but the word itself names God's verdict.

decisions.choice: be put right with God (R); be justified (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Justify" is a key word of the letter and stays at Literal and Balanced. Readable says what it means in plain words: put right with God, the one who gives the verdict.

decisions.choice: like a guardian, the servant who was put in charge of a child
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the guardian was (meaning note m1), since English has no single word for him. It says "servant", as the style guide has it; m1 keeps that he was a household slave.

decisions.choice: until the coming of Christ (B); until Christ came (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the time meaning of "until Christ" (meaning note m2).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting: "Christ" by default, "Messiah" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: guía (L, B); un guía, el siervo encargado de cuidar a un niño (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "pedagogo" now means an educator, the sense meaning note m1 sets aside; "ayo", the older word for a child's attendant, is no longer understood; "tutor" is a legal guardian, the figure of 4:2. "Guía" names someone who escorts and supervises, and Readable explains who he was, as the English does.

decisions.choice: justificados (L, B); Dios pudo declararnos justos (R)
decisions.reason: As in Romans: Literal and Balanced keep "justificar", the letter's key verb; Readable says what it means, God's verdict that declares someone in the right (meaning note m3).

decisions.choice: mlezi (every level); R adds "yule mtumishi aliyewekwa kumtunza mtoto"
decisions.reason: "Mlezi" is the one who brings up and looks after a child, which is what the household slave did (meaning note m1); "mwalimu" would make him a teacher, which he was not. Readable explains who he was, as the English does.

decisions.choice: tuhesabiwe haki (every level)
decisions.reason: As in Romans, "kuhesabiwa haki" (to be counted righteous) is kept at every level: it already says that justification is God's verdict, and Readable adds "na Mungu" where the English says "put right with God".

decisions.choice: gardien (L, B, and 3:25); le serviteur chargé de surveiller un enfant (R)
decisions.reason: The word was the household slave who watched over a boy, not his teacher (m1). French "pédagogue" comes from it but now means an educator, and "précepteur" a private tutor; "tuteur" is kept for the legal guardian of 4:2. "Gardien" also fits the custody of verse 23.

source.text: ἐλθούσης δὲ τῆς πίστεως οὐκέτι ὑπὸ παιδαγωγόν ἐσμεν.

records.literal_gloss: Having come and the faith, no longer under guardian we are.

en.L: But the faith having come, we are no longer under a guardian.
en.B: Faith has now come, and we are no longer in the care of a guardian.
en.R: But now the time of faith has come, and we are not under that guardian any longer.

es.L: Pero habiendo venido la fe, ya no estamos bajo [un] guía.
es.B: La fe ya ha llegado, y ya no estamos al cuidado de un guía.
es.R: Pero ahora ha llegado el tiempo de la fe, y ya no estamos bajo ese guía.

sw.L: Lakini imani ikiisha kuja, hatuko tena chini ya mlezi.
sw.B: Imani sasa imekuja, nasi hatuko tena chini ya uangalizi wa mlezi.
sw.R: Lakini sasa wakati wa imani umefika, na hatuko tena chini ya mlezi yule.

fr.L: Mais la foi étant venue, nous ne sommes plus sous un gardien.
fr.B: Maintenant que la foi est venue, nous ne sommes plus confiés à un gardien.
fr.R: Mais maintenant, le temps de la foi est venu, et nous ne sommes plus sous ce gardien.

decisions.choice: now that faith has come: the time of the guardian is over
alternatives: whenever a person comes to faith
decisions.reason: The words take up "before the faith came" in verse 23: the coming of faith is the arrival of Christ in history, and with it the end of the law's role as guardian. Each believer enters that new time by faith (verse 26).

decisions.choice: the time of faith
decisions.reason: As in verse 23.

decisions.choice: in the care of a guardian
decisions.reason: The guardian was a carer and supervisor (verse 24, meaning note m1); Balanced says what being "under" him meant.

source.text: πάντες γὰρ υἱοὶ θεοῦ ἐστε διὰ τῆς πίστεως ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: All for sons of God you are through the faith in Christ Jesus.

en.L: For you are all {{gender:children|sons}} of God through the faith, in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.
en.B: For in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus you are all {{gender:children|sons}} of God, through faith.
en.R: All of you are God's {{gender:children|sons}} through faith, because you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

es.L: Porque todos {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} hijos de Dios por medio de la fe, en {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} Jesús.
es.B: Porque en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} Jesús todos {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} hijos de Dios, por medio de la fe.
es.R: Todos {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} hijos de Dios por la fe, porque {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} Jesús.

sw.L: Kwa maana ninyi nyote ni wana wa Mungu kupitia ile imani, katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.
sw.B: Kwa maana katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu ninyi nyote ni wana wa Mungu, kupitia imani.
sw.R: Ninyi nyote ni wana wa Mungu kwa njia ya imani, kwa sababu ninyi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.

fr.L: Car vous êtes tous {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Dieu par la foi, {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus.
fr.B: Car {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, vous êtes tous {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Dieu, par la foi.
fr.R: Vous êtes tous des {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Dieu par la foi, parce que vous appartenez au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus.

decisions.choice: sons of God: the status of a son and heir, given to women and men alike
alternatives: children in a general sense, without the right of the heir
decisions.reason: In Paul's world it was the son who inherited, and the word carries that status: verse 29 calls these sons "heirs", and 4:1-7 develops the picture. Paul gives this status to all believers, since in Christ there is "male and female" alike (verse 28). The Greek word is masculine, but its point is the standing of the heir, not the sex of the believer.

decisions.choice: in Christ Jesus goes with "you are sons": you are God's sons in union with Christ, through faith
alternatives: faith in Christ Jesus, with Christ as the one believed in
decisions.reason: Paul rarely uses "in" for the one in whom faith is placed. The next two verses speak of being baptized into Christ and of being one "in Christ Jesus", so here too "in Christ Jesus" most likely says where believers are: joined to him. Faith is the means, union with Christ the place.

decisions.choice: you all: Paul turns from "we" to "you", including the Gentile believers of Galatia
decisions.reason: After "we" in verses 23-25, Paul now addresses the Galatians directly. Gentiles who were never under the law are God's sons on the same footing.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The default is inclusive, because Paul applies the status to all believers (meaning note m1); "sons" keeps the word of the heir. The footnote explains the difference.

decisions.choice: in Christ Jesus placed first
decisions.reason: Putting "in Christ Jesus" first keeps it from being read as the object of faith (meaning note m2).

decisions.choice: because you belong to Christ Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what being "in" Christ means here: joined to him and belonging to him (verse 29).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting: "Christ" by default, "Messiah" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: hijos, no setting
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" means both sons and children, so it carries the heir's status (meaning note m1) and includes the daughters at once; the English needs a setting for this, the Spanish does not.

decisions.choice: wana, no setting
decisions.reason: "Wana" is used of sons and daughters alike and keeps the status of the heir that 4:1-7 develops; "watoto" would lose it. So the Swahili has no gender setting.

source.text: ὅσοι γὰρ εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε, Χριστὸν ἐνεδύσασθε·

records.literal_gloss: As many as for into Christ you were baptized, Christ you put on.

en.L: For as many [of you] as were baptized into {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, you clothed yourselves with {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Every one of you who was baptized into {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has put on {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} like clothing.
en.R: All of you who were baptized and joined to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} have put on {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, like a set of new clothes.

es.L: Porque cuantos {{plural_you:fueron bautizados|fuisteis bautizados}} en {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, de {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} {{plural_you:se revistieron|os revestisteis}}.
es.B: Todos los que {{plural_you:han|habéis}} sido bautizados en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} {{plural_you:se han revestido|os habéis revestido}} {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} como de una prenda.
es.R: Todos los que {{plural_you:fueron|fuisteis}} bautizados y unidos {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} {{plural_you:se han revestido|os habéis revestido}} {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, como quien se pone ropa nueva.

sw.L: Kwa maana wote mliobatizwa kuingia katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, mlimvaa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Kila mmoja wenu aliyebatizwa kuingia katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} amemvaa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kama vazi.
sw.R: Ninyi nyote mliobatizwa na kuunganishwa na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} mmemvaa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kama nguo mpya.

fr.L: Car vous tous qui avez été baptisés {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}, vous avez revêtu {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.B: Vous tous qui avez été baptisés {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}, vous avez revêtu le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} comme un vêtement.
fr.R: Vous tous qui avez été baptisés et unis au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, vous vous êtes revêtus du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, comme d’habits neufs.

decisions.choice: baptized into Christ: baptized into union with him
alternatives: baptized in the name of Christ only
decisions.reason: Baptism "into" Christ marks the start of belonging to him and sharing in his death and life (Romans 6:3-4; 1 Corinthians 12:13). It explains how believers come to be "in Christ Jesus" (verse 26).

decisions.choice: put on Christ: take him on like a garment, so that one's identity is his
decisions.reason: To "put on" a person was to take on that person's character and role. Paul uses the picture for what happened at baptism, and also calls believers to live it out (Romans 13:14; compare Colossians 3:9-10). The clothing image leads into verse 28: under the one garment the old marks of standing no longer divide.

decisions.choice: like clothing (B); like a set of new clothes (R)
decisions.reason: "Put on Christ" is unclear in modern English; the comparison makes the picture plain.

decisions.choice: baptized and joined to Christ
decisions.reason: Readable explains "into" (meaning note m1).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting: "Christ" by default, "Messiah" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: revestirse de
decisions.reason: Spanish "revestirse de" is the verb for putting on a garment and also for taking on a quality, so it carries both sides of the picture (meaning note m2) at every level.

source.text: οὐκ ἔνι Ἰουδαῖος οὐδὲ Ἕλλην, οὐκ ἔνι δοῦλος οὐδὲ ἐλεύθερος, οὐκ ἔνι ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ· πάντες γὰρ ὑμεῖς εἷς ἐστε ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Not there is Jew nor Greek, not there is slave nor free, not there is male and female; all for you one are in Christ Jesus.

en.L: There is not Jew nor Greek, there is not slave nor free, there is not male and female; for all you are one in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.
en.B: There is no Jew or Greek, there is no slave or free person, there is no male and female, for all of you are one in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.
en.R: Being a Jew or a Gentile, a slave or a free person, a man or a woman, does not divide you. All of you are one in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

es.L: No hay judío ni griego, no hay esclavo ni libre, no hay varón y hembra; porque todos {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} uno en {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} Jesús.
es.B: No hay judío ni griego, no hay esclavo ni libre, no hay varón y hembra, porque todos {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} uno en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} Jesús.
es.R: Ser judío o no judío, esclavo o libre, hombre o mujer, no {{plural_you:los|os}} divide. Todos {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} uno en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} Jesús.

sw.L: Hakuna Myahudi wala Mgiriki, hakuna mtumwa wala [mtu] huru, hakuna mwanamume na mwanamke; kwa maana ninyi nyote ni mmoja katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.
sw.B: Hakuna Myahudi wala Mgiriki, hakuna mtumwa wala mtu huru, hakuna mwanamume na mwanamke, kwa maana ninyi nyote ni mmoja katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.
sw.R: Kuwa Myahudi au mtu asiye Myahudi, mtumwa au mtu huru, mwanamume au mwanamke, hakuwagawanyi. Ninyi nyote mmekuwa mtu mmoja katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.

fr.L: Il n’y a ni Juif ni Grec, il n’y a ni esclave ni libre, il n’y a pas mâle et femelle ; car vous tous, vous êtes un {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus.
fr.B: Il n’y a ni Juif ni Grec, il n’y a ni esclave ni personne libre, il n’y a pas homme et femme, car vous tous, vous ne faites qu’un {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus.
fr.R: Être juif ou non juif, esclave ou libre, homme ou femme, cela ne vous divise pas. Vous tous, vous ne faites qu’un {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus.

decisions.choice: in Christ these distinctions give no one a different standing: all are one
alternatives: the differences themselves cease to exist
a statement about spiritual equality with no effect on how believers live together
decisions.reason: The three pairs were the great divisions of the ancient world, by race, by social position and by sex. In Christ none of them gives anyone a higher or lower place among God's children and heirs (verses 26 and 29). Paul still speaks to Jews and Gentiles, slaves and masters, men and women as such (1 Corinthians 7:17-24), but in Galatians the first pair has direct consequences: Gentiles need not become Jews, and Jewish believers may not separate from them at the table (2:11-14). Colossians 3:11 has a similar list.

decisions.choice: male and female: the words of Genesis 1:27
decisions.reason: The first two pairs use "nor"; the third uses "and", the wording of Genesis 1:27 in the Greek Old Testament, "male and female he made them". The new creation in Christ (6:15) does not divide along the line drawn in the first creation.

decisions.choice: Greek: a Gentile, anyone who is not a Jew
decisions.reason: Paired with "Jew", Ἕλλην stands for all non-Jews, as in Romans 1:16. The Galatians themselves were not Greeks by birth.

decisions.choice: one: one person, one body, in Christ
decisions.reason: εἷς is masculine: believers are together one new person in Christ, the one offspring of Abraham (verses 16 and 29; compare Ephesians 2:15). Unity here is not agreement but belonging to one body.

decisions.choice: Gentile (R); Greek (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense the pair has (meaning note m3).

decisions.choice: does not divide you
decisions.reason: Readable says what "there is not" means for the church (meaning note m1); it does not say the differences have disappeared.

decisions.choice: a man or a woman
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the pair; Literal and Balanced keep "male and female", which echo Genesis 1:27.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting: "Christ" by default, "Messiah" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: varón y hembra (L, B); hombre o mujer (R)
decisions.reason: "Varón y hembra" is the familiar Spanish wording of Genesis 1:27, which Paul echoes (meaning note m2). On its own "hembra" now sounds like a word for animals, so a reviewer may prefer "hombre y mujer" at Balanced.

decisions.choice: mwanamume na mwanamke (L, B); mwanamume au mwanamke (R)
decisions.reason: Swahili has no separate pair for male and female people: "dume" and "jike" are used of animals, and "mume" and "mke" mean husband and wife. So every level uses "mwanamume" and "mwanamke", and the echo of Genesis 1:27 rests on the meaning note.

decisions.choice: mmekuwa mtu mmoja
decisions.reason: Readable says "one person", the sense of the masculine "one" (meaning note m4), so that "mmoja" is not read as "of one mind".

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free.

decisions.choice: mâle et femelle (L); homme et femme (B, R)
decisions.reason: The third pair has "and" where the others have "nor", the wording of Genesis 1:27 (m2). Literal keeps the Greek words; in modern French "mâle et femelle" is said of animals, so Balanced says "homme et femme", the French of Genesis 1:27, keeping the "et".

decisions.choice: esclave at every level
decisions.reason: Slave is set against free here, so every level keeps "esclave", as the style guide and the English do.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ὑμεῖς Χριστοῦ, ἄρα τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ σπέρμα ἐστέ, κατ’ ἐπαγγελίαν κληρονόμοι.

records.literal_gloss: If and you of Christ, then of the Abraham seed you are, according to promise heirs.

en.L: And if you [are] of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, then you are Abraham's seed, heirs according to promise.
en.B: And if you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, it follows that you are Abraham's offspring, heirs in keeping with the promise.
en.R: If you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, then you are Abraham's offspring too. You are heirs who will receive what God promised.

es.L: Y si {{plural_you:ustedes [son]|vosotros [sois]}} {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, entonces {{plural_you:son|sois}} simiente de Abraham, herederos según [la] promesa.
es.B: Y si {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, se sigue que {{plural_you:son|sois}} descendencia de Abraham, herederos conforme a la promesa.
es.R: Si {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, entonces también {{plural_you:son|sois}} descendencia de Abraham. {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} herederos que recibirán lo que Dios prometió.

sw.L: Na ikiwa ninyi [ni] wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, basi ninyi ni uzao wa Ibrahimu, warithi kwa kadiri ya ahadi.
sw.B: Na ikiwa ninyi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, basi ninyi ni uzao wa Ibrahimu, warithi kwa mujibu wa ahadi.
sw.R: Kama ninyi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, basi ninyi pia ni uzao wa Ibrahimu. Ninyi ni warithi mtakaopokea kile ambacho Mungu aliahidi.

fr.L: Et si vous [êtes] du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, alors vous êtes descendance d’Abraham, héritiers selon la promesse.
fr.B: Et si vous appartenez au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, alors vous êtes la descendance d’Abraham, héritiers selon la promesse.
fr.R: Si vous appartenez au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, alors vous êtes, vous aussi, les descendants d’Abraham. Vous êtes des héritiers qui recevront ce que Dieu a promis.

decisions.choice: belonging to Christ, the one seed, makes believers Abraham's seed
alternatives: believers become Abraham's descendants by physical birth or by circumcision
decisions.reason: In verse 16 the one seed is Christ. Those who belong to him are included in him, so they are Abraham's seed too, though many and though Gentiles. Paul keeps the singular σπέρμα with a plural "you": all of them together are the one offspring in Christ. This answers the claim that Gentiles must be circumcised to belong to Abraham's family.

decisions.choice: heirs: those who will receive the inheritance God promised
decisions.reason: The inheritance of verse 18 comes by promise, not by the law, and it goes to heirs. Paul develops the picture of the heir in 4:1-7.

decisions.choice: seed (L); offspring (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 16.

decisions.choice: belong to Christ
decisions.reason: The genitive means belonging; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: heirs who will receive what God promised
decisions.reason: Readable explains what an heir "according to promise" receives.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting: "Christ" by default, "Messiah" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: descendencia (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the singular "seed" is said of the many believers together (meaning note m1). The collective "descendencia" keeps the singular and includes them all; verse 16 needed "descendiente" to point to one person.

decisions.choice: uzao (every level)
decisions.reason: Here the singular "seed" is said of the many believers together (meaning note m1). The collective "uzao" keeps the singular and includes them all; verses 16 and 19 needed "mzao" to point to one person.
